- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in true price, model often overcorrects downward; apply a 2–5% lagged overshoot correction to avoid premature decline.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model tends to underpredict downside; add 2–5% buffer below forecast to account for bearish sentiment drag.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast range by 1–3% to reflect event-driven noise.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes (e.g., 1.00 values), model tends to underestimate peak; apply a 1–3% upward bias to peak days.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true price in early days of a 30d window, apply a 1–2% upward shift to account for mean reversion bias.  
- In low-event periods (≤15 events/30d), model often overestimates stability; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1% to reflect reduced volatility.
